Also, let $a, b, c$ be three functions of $x, y, z$ satisfying the
condition
$$\frac{d a}{d x}+\frac{d b}{d y}+\frac{d c}{d z}=0$$
(25)
and let
$$\left.\begin{array}{l}
a=-r_{1} \frac{d V}{d x}+u \\
b=-r_{2} \frac{d V}{d y}+v \\
c=-r_{3} \frac{d V}{d z}+w .
\end{array}\right\}$$
(26)
Finally, let the triple-integral
$$W=\iiint\left(R_{1} a^{2}+R_{2} b^{2}+R_{3} c^{2}\right) d x d y d z$$
(27)
be extended over spaces bounded as in the enunciation of Art.
$100 a$; such viz. that over certain portions $V$ is constant or else
the normal component of the vector $a, b, c$ is given, the former
condition being accompanied by the further restriction that the
integral of this component over the whole bounding surface
must be zero : then $W$ will be a minimum when
$$u=0, \quad v=0, \quad v=0 .$$
For we have in this case
$$r_{1} R_{1}=1, \quad r_{2} R_{2}=1, \quad r_{3} R_{3}=1 ;$$
and therefore, by (26),
$$\begin{aligned}
W & =\iiint\left(\left.r_{1} \frac{d \bar{V}}{d x}\right|^{2}+\left.r_{2} \frac{\overline{d V}^{2}}{d y}\right|^{2}+\left.r_{3} \frac{\overline{d V}^{2}}{d z}\right|^{2}\right) d x d y d z \\
& +\iiint\left(R_{1} u^{2}+R_{2} v^{2}+R_{3} w^{2}\right) d x d y d z \\
& -2 \iiint\left(u \frac{d V}{d x}+v \frac{d V}{d y}+w \frac{d V}{d z}\right) d x d y d z
\end{aligned}$$
(28)
But since
$$\frac{d u}{d x}+\frac{d v}{d y}+\frac{d w}{d z}=0$$
(29)
the third term vanishes by virtue of the conditions at the limits.
The first term of (28) is therefore the unique minimum value
of $W$.

 integral of this component over the whole bounding surface

$$u=0, \quad v=0, \quad v=0 .$$

$$r_{1} R_{1}=1, \quad r_{2} R_{2}=1, \quad r_{3} R_{3}=1 ;$$

$$\begin{align*}
W & =\iiint\left(\left.r_{1} \frac{d \bar{V}}{d x}\right|^{2}+\left.r_{2} \frac{\overline{d V}^{2}}{d y}\right|^{2}+\left.r_{3} \frac{\overline{d V}^{2}}{d z}\right|^{2}\right) d x d y d z \\
& +\iiint\left(R_{1} u^{2}+R_{2} v^{2}+R_{3} w^{2}\right) d x d y d z \\

\end{align*}$$


But since

$$\begin{equation*}
\frac{d u}{d x}+\frac{d v}{d y}+\frac{d w}{d z}=0 \tag{29}
\end{equation*}$$

the third term vanishes by virtue of the conditions at the limits.

The first term of (28) is therefore the unique minimum value
 of $W$.
